object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who receives medical care at the clinic, identified by a unique patient ID.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient
Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a patient, printed on their card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who sees patients at the clinic, identified by a unique license number.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments.
Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a doctor's medical license.

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled meeting between a patient and a doctor at the clinic, identified by an appointment number.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments.
Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to an appointment when it is created.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room at the clinic where appointments take place, identified by a room number.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for an exam room.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical specialty such as cardiology or general practice.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: Date
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment is scheduled.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time interval during the day when appointments are booked, such as 09:00 or 09:30.

source_references.excerpt: we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current state of an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason given by the patient for their appointment, provided at the time of booking.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A note attached by the doctor after the appointment with follow-up information.

ambiguities.description: Scheduling constraint completeness: The transcript states appointments are scheduled on a date and time slot, but does not explicitly address whether the same patient can have multiple appointments at the same date and time slot, or whether the same doctor can see multiple patients at the same date and time slot. Current model allows these collisions. Question: Should there be a uniqueness constraint preventing double-booking (one appointment per date-time-slot globally, or per doctor, or per patient)?

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: Exam room assignment: Exam rooms are mentioned and identified by room number, but the transcript does not specify whether appointments are assigned to exam rooms, or whether exam rooms participate in any relationship. Question: Is an exam room assigned to each appointment, and if so, is this mandatory or optional? Can an exam room host multiple appointments?

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

ambiguities.description: Visit reason optionality verification: The transcript states 'An appointment can have a visit reason', which suggests optionality. However, it is not explicitly stated whether every visit reason in the system must be used on at least one appointment. Question: Is visit reason participation optional on the appointment side only, or is there also a reverse mandatory (every recorded visit reason must be attached to an appointment)?

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

ambiguities.description: Follow-up note attachment authority: The transcript states 'after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note', which implies the doctor role but does not explicitly model the attachment action. Question: Should there be a separate fact type capturing which doctor attaches which follow-up note to which appointment (e.g., 'Doctor attaches FollowUpNote to Appointment')? Currently, FollowUpNote is modeled as a simple attribute value, not as an entity.

source_references.excerpt: after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note

ambiguities.description: Primary doctor versus appointment doctor distinction: The transcript clarifies that a patient's primary doctor 'is separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment' (lines 29-31). While this distinction is clear conceptually, there is no explicit business rule stated (e.g., must the primary doctor always be available, or can the primary doctor ever see the patient in an appointment?). Question: Are there any constraints linking the primary doctor to the appointment doctor -- for instance, can a patient only be seen by doctors of the same specialty as their primary doctor, or is there no connection?

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.
